instructions: Cut the 4 corn tortillas into thin strips and set them aside.
Heat 2 tbsp of the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Dice the onion, add 1/3 cup of it and cook for 3 minutes, until soft. Mince the garlic, add it and cook for 1 minute.
Add 1 tsp of the ancho chili powder, the cumin, the oregano and 3/4 tsp of the salt. Stir for 30 seconds, until you can smell the spices.
In a blender, combine the tomatoes with their juice, the beans with their liquid and 1 cup of the broth. Blend in two batches until mostly smooth, with a little texture left.

Pour the blended soup into the pot. Rinse the blender with the remaining 1 1/2 cups broth and add that too. Bring to a simmer, then turn the heat to medium-low and partly cover. Stand back a little. It will spatter. Simmer for 25 minutes, stirring now and then.

While the soup simmers, heat the remaining 3 tbsp oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tortilla strips in two batches for 1 to 2 minutes each, until golden and crisp. Transfer them to a plate lined with paper towels and sprinkle with the remaining 1/4 tsp salt.
Slice the avocado and crumble the queso fresco.
Taste the soup. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Ladle the soup into bowls. Top each with a spoonful of the crema, some queso fresco, the fried tortilla strips and the avocado, then sprinkle with the remaining 1/2 tsp ancho chili powder.
method_notes: Lead is Flavor Mosaic (5 from 6 ratings), a canned tomato and pinto bean soup; fewer than 20 ratings, so this is a fallback lead. The PBS version roasts fresh tomatoes and soaks whole ancho chiles instead of using powder, and fries the tortilla strips, which is borrowed here. Both blend the beans with part of the broth and finish with crema, cotija or queso fresco, avocado and fried tortilla. Vegetable broth is used so the soup stays vegetarian, and the quantities are scaled from 6 servings to 4.
